title: ASP.NET Core Complete Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API: controllers, routing, model binding, validation, middleware, DI, configuration, filters, and authentication.

data.text: Project Structure
ASP.NET Core apps start in `Program.cs`. The minimal hosting model registers services, configures middleware, and starts the app.

data.title: Program.cs Minimal Hosting Model

data.text: MVC Controllers
Controllers handle HTTP requests. Inherit from `Controller` for views or `ControllerBase` for APIs. Use attributes for routing.

data.title: MVC Controller with Views
Web API Controller

data.text: Routing
Routing maps URLs to controllers/actions. Use conventional routing for MVC and attribute routing for APIs.

data.title: Conventional vs Attribute Routing

data.text: Model Binding and Validation
Model binding maps request data to action parameters. Validation attributes enforce rules automatically.

data.title: Model Binding Sources and Validation

data.text: Middleware Pipeline
Middleware processes requests and responses in order. Use `Use`, `Run`, and `Map` to build the pipeline.

data.title: Custom Middleware and Ordering

data.text: Dependency Injection
ASP.NET Core has a built-in DI container. Register services with `AddTransient`, `AddScoped`, or `AddSingleton`.

data.title: Service Lifetimes and Injection

data.text: Configuration
Configuration comes from `appsettings.json`, environment variables, user secrets, and command-line args. The options pattern provides strongly-typed settings.

data.title: Options Pattern and appsettings.json

data.text: Filters
Filters run code before or after specific pipeline stages: authorization, action execution, exceptions, and results.

data.title: Action Filter and Exception Filter

data.text: Authentication and Authorization
Use `[Authorize]` to protect endpoints. Supports JWT, cookies, and external providers like Google.

data.title: JWT Authentication Setup

data.text: CORS
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) allows or blocks requests from different origins. Configure policies in `Program.cs`.

data.title: CORS Policy Configuration

data.text: Response Types and Status Codes
Return proper HTTP status codes using `IActionResult` helpers. APIs should use `ActionResult<T>` for automatic 200/201/400/404/500 handling.

data.title: Common IActionResult Returns
